title: SHRDLU documented in Winograd's 1972 rewritten account
summary: In a later first-person account, Terry Winograd states that his original SHRDLU dissertation was Winograd (1971) and that Winograd (1972) was a rewritten version. The same paper describes SHRDLU as answering questions, carrying out commands, incorporating new facts about its world, and operating in a simulated blocks world.
significance: A safely documented publication/history milestone for SHRDLU. LINEAiGE records the 1972 rewritten-account milestone and does not infer an exact implementation date, system-birth date, first-ever status, geography, ancestry, influence, causality, or relationship edges from this evidence alone.

verification.note: Primary claim evidence is Terry Winograd's own retrospective paper hosted by Stanford HCI. It explicitly distinguishes the original 1971 dissertation from the 1972 rewritten version and describes SHRDLU's question answering, command execution, fact incorporation, and simulated-world behavior. A Stanford course source independently corroborates the 1972 SHRDLU reference. The candidate deliberately withholds invention, completion, priority, geographic, causal, and lineage claims.
